full_judgment:
2. The matter arises from a Certificate Sale held in November 1964 in Certificate Case No. 20898 / 63-64. A landed property which had belonged to Gram Sharkar and others was sold in auction in that certificate case for arrear of rent and it was purchased by one Rustom Ali and others who went into possession and thereafter sold it to the Plaintiffs-respondents. The Respondents have been in possession of the land constructing dwelling houses, but 16 years later, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (One of the defendants—Petitioners) by an order dated 23 August 1982, cancelled the Certificate Sale taking the view that the Certificate-debtores were Indian nationals and as such their property was an enemy property, subsequently vested property, which could not have been sold by certificate procedure. This order of cancellation was challenged by the Plaintiffs- respondents by filing O.C. Suit No. 210 of 1982. After contest, the suit was decreed by the Subordinate Judge on 10 August 1983. The Defendants filed an appeal hit the appeal also was dismissed, on contest, by the Additional District Judge (Mr. Ruhul Amin) on 10 July 1984. Before his successor in-office (Mr. Salahuddin Mahmood), defendants filed an application for review of the judgment and decree of his predecessor, Additional District Judge. This application for review was allowed on merit of the case and the Judgment and decree was set aside. Plaintiffs successfully challenged this order by filing Civil Revision No. 785 of 1988. The learned Single Judge held that the grounds taken in the review petition and considered by the successor Additional District Judge were beyond the scope of Order XLVII, Rule 2 of the Civil Procedure Code. 

 3. Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the petitioners, has submitted that the review application was filed by genuine mistake and that the Defendants-petitioners should be given a chance to question the validity of the decree in appropriate forum. It appears that the learned Successor-Additional District Judge entered deep into the merit of the case, as if he were hearing an appeal from the Judgment of his predecessor, Additional District Judge. It has been rightly pointed out by the learned Single Judge that the application for review was on grounds "other than the discovery of new and important matters or the existence of any clerical mistake or error apparent on the face of the decree" as specified in Rule 2 of Order XLVII C.P.C.
